correctness.rationale: Direct endpoint integration reduces every nonzero root to equality of two sine amplitudes with a unit phase. Their equal magnitudes force an integral phase sum or difference, giving precisely three explicit integer/odd-parity lattices. Differentiation rules out multiple roots except when both sine factors vanish at equal widths; the explicit sine–cosine factorization gives exactly order two there. Reduced rational arithmetic proves each family's existence criterion. Wiener's L1/L2 translation criteria and the measure/category argument complete the conclusions. The 9,000-case finite checker only supplements this complete analytic proof.
